tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

files.description: File paths (absolute or relative to cwd) to send to the user. Always pass an array, even for a single file.

caption.description: Optional short caption for the file(s).

status.description: Use 'proactive' when you're surfacing a file the user hasn't asked for and needs to see now — a generated artifact, a completed report. Use 'normal' when replying to something the user just said.

display.description: How the client should present the file. 'render' opens it inline in the side panel (for HTML, SVG, Mermaid, images, PDFs — anything the user wants to look at now). 'attach' shows a download card only, no inline preview (for deliverables the user will save and open elsewhere). Omit to let the client decide by file type — today that means renderable types render and everything else attaches, same as before this parameter existed.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

# Handoff to the next session

State on 2026-10-11, about 06:30. Read `CLAUDE.md` first, then `changes.md` section "UI alignment" (U.1 to U.24): it records every decision of this session with its reason. **Nothing of this session is committed.**

## 1. Do first: finish populating Supabase

State at the end of the session (2026-10-11, about 09:00):

- Supabase has migrations 0001 to 0016, the seed (10,128 verbatims, 13,771 signals, 13,404 with an embedding) and **1,657 cases from a build that failed in its last step**. Those cases have a page but no figures, no tags, no open state, no scores. There is no search index and there are no users.
- The build failed because the last step wrote all cases in one long transaction and Supabase closed the connection. That step now commits every 25 cases (`backend/app/cases/pipeline.py`, `WRITE_BATCH`).
- The user then decided a stricter rule (`changes.md` is not updated for it yet): a group of signals becomes a case only with **20 distinct customers** whose feedback is at least as much complaint or wish as praise, or **10 distinct customers reporting a defect**, in one BMW line, or with competitor evidence. A group below the bar becomes **no case** (nothing written, tagged or stored); its signals wait without a case. Counted on Supabase this keeps 48 cases (17 / 13 / 22 for the 5 / 7 / 1 Series) holding 1,676 signals. The user rejected redefining a signal as a bundle of five reports.
- Commit `9f370f0` holds this rule, the batching, the reset script and the LLM cache of the build. **None of it has been run or tested.**

Steps, in this order. Ask the user before each one that touches Supabase or OpenAI.

1. `cd backend && uv run pytest` (offline, about 4 minutes). One test in `tests/test_cases.py` was rewritten for the new rule and never run; other assertions in that file may need the same adjustment. Fix until green.
2. `uv run python -m app.cases.reset` (dry run: prints what people have worked on and the number of cases; every count except `cases` must be 0).
3. `uv run python -m app.cases.reset --yes`: removes every case on Supabase and sets the opening rule on every config. Signals are kept and only lose their case. It refuses when a person has worked on a case. Not reversible.
4. `LLM_WORKERS=12 uv run python -m app.demo build`: skips the finished seed and the embedded signals, groups again under the new rule, then figures, tags, scores, search index, demo users. The case pages and tags of the groups that stay are in the LLM cache (`backend/.data/llm_cache`), so the only new OpenAI cost should be the embeddings of the search index (about 13,000 short texts). Expect minutes, not hours: 48 cases instead of 1,657.
5. Check: `select count(*) from case_item` (about 48), `select vehicle, state, count(*) from case_vehicle group by 1, 2`, a few case pages, `select count(*) from case_score`, `select count(*) from rag_chunk`, `select count(*) from app_user` (8), `select pg_size_pretty(pg_database_size(current_database()))` (was 201 MB before the reset; the limit is 500 MB).

If step 4 fails: read the last rows of `agent_run` (a row left on `running` with no process behind it is dead: set it to `failed`), then run the same command again. Finished steps are skipped and no LLM answer is paid twice. The search index step embeds inside one transaction; if that is the step that drops, run `uv run python -m app.rag.index` on its own.

Do not run `app.demo e2e` on Supabase: it confirms and approves a case in the real data.

## 2. What this session changed

**Schema (new migrations, never edit an applied one):**
- `0014_ui_alignment.sql`: 15 tables and many columns for what the UI shows (briefs, stances, questions, meeting notes, proposals, referrals, innovation pool, comments, alerts, vehicle plan, requirement versions / feedback / checks, owners and workflow per case and line, sign-off statuses).
- `0015_rag_pm_context.sql`: the search index may hold PM context.
- `0016_size_budget.sql`: two vector indexes dropped, embeddings stored with 768 dimensions (`EMBEDDING_DIM`), `rag_search` takes a vector of any size.
- Supabase has all 16. **The local database has 0001 to 0015 only.** Applying 0016 locally clears its embeddings and its search index; they must be rebuilt after (`python -m app.signals.embed`, `python -m app.rag.index`).

**Pipeline and agents:**
- Prompts `case_writer@v2`, `case_tags@v2`, `requirement_writer@v2`, `rag_agent@v2`. Tried against OpenAI: case writer and case tags (good output on three real cases). **Never run against OpenAI: `requirement_writer@v2` and `rag_agent@v2`.**
- Models and thinking effort (`app/config.py`): gpt-6-luna with effort `low` for `feedback_classify`, `signal_extract`, `case_writer`, `case_tags`; gpt-6-luna with the default effort for the RAG agent; gpt-6.1-sol with the default effort for `requirement_writer`. gpt-6-luna has no `minimal` effort (the API accepts none, low, medium, high, xhigh).
- The LLM never works inside a database transaction any more (seed, case pipeline, backfill). The three earlier Supabase attempts failed in `seed:feedback` with dropped connections while the connection waited on the LLM.
- Observed cases are not scored; a case is scored when it opens. Machine events are not indexed for the RAG agent; the PM context is.
- Fetch loop: a record the LLM finds nothing in keeps only a marker row (relevance filter). YouTube: videos of the last 60 days, the 10 most relevant comments per video. Wikipedia and Wikidata are called as official APIs (robots.txt refused them before).

**API and UI:**
- About 40 new endpoints in `backend/app/api/routers/workspace.py`, services in `backend/app/collab/`.
- The adapter in `web/src/backend/` serves all 67 endpoints of the UI contract from the API (`DATA_SOURCE=backend`). The JSON sidecar and the persona table are gone; users are `app_user` rows.
- UI fixes: brief page on a brief pre-filled from data, drag and drop on the case board, readable audit lines and proposal cards (`web/src/lib/audit.ts`).

## 3. Decisions made in this session

Each one is also a row of `changes.md` (U.1 to U.24). "User" = decided by the user in the session; "Claude" = proposed and applied by the assistant, not objected to.

| Decision | Why | By |
|---|---|---|
| Fit schema, agents and API to the UI before the Supabase migration and the paid run | Otherwise the case pages would be paid for twice | User |
| The adapter serves the whole UI contract from the API; mock and real data are never mixed; the sidecar file is gone | The earlier adapter showed mock cases next to real signals | Claude |
| The case lifecycle keeps its four states; the PM's steps are `workflow`, the decision is `outcome` | The UI has six states and six outcomes; the documented lifecycle stays the source of truth | Claude |
| Cases are owned per line; handing a case over never copies it | A copy would split the evidence | Claude |
| Requirements hold structured fields, the page is rendered from them, every change is a version | The UI edits SMART fields, not markdown | User (guide 8.5) |
| Statuses signed off, planned and exported exist in the backend; only the head signs off | Guide 8.5 | User (guide 8.5) |
| Confirming a case does not draft from the UI; the shape questions come first | UI layer 3 | Claude |
| Brand fit stays a multiplier, `reach` stays a factor; the UI's "project type" setting is not stored | Scoring decisions of `CLAUDE.md` are not changed for the UI | Claude |
| The RAG agent knows the PM context and cites it apart from customer evidence | It could not say what engineering answered | User |
| On a case that spans lines the agent uses only the brief of the asking PM's line | The 7 Series brief appeared on a 5 Series case | User |
| Load the database from BMW's original files, not from the processed CSVs | Same content; the originals keep sheet and row; the processed option lists lose the columns | User, after the assistant's advice |
| BMW feedback that is not relevant is kept out of cases, scores and the index, not deleted | All verbatims are 2.2 MB; deleting breaks the counts and the transparency | Assistant's advice; the user raised the point and did not overrule it |
| A fetched web record without a relevant statement keeps only a marker row | Space and noise | User |
| Size budget for the free plan: no vector index on `signal` and `rag_chunk`, 768 dimensions, no scores for observed cases, no machine events in the search index | The local build was 789 MB, the plan allows 500 MB | User asked for a solution; measures by Claude |
| gpt-6-luna with thinking `low` for classification, extraction, case pages and tags; default thinking for the RAG agent; gpt-6.1-sol with default thinking for requirements | Reading tasks need little reasoning. The user asked for "minimal", the model does not offer it; "none" was tried and the user chose "low" | User |
| YouTube: videos of the last 2 months, 10 comments per video, comments and transcripts | A few strong, recent voices per video | User |
| Keep the mock in the repository as the offline fallback | Demo safety; the adapter reuses its deterministic logic | Assistant's advice, not objected to |
| Migrations 0014 to 0016 applied on Supabase and the build started with OpenAI | "Now try to migrate the work to Supabase"; "run the Supabase migration using OpenAI" | User |

Not decided yet (ask the user): running the YouTube fetch into Supabase; what to do about the 1 GB storage limit before a web backfill; whether `case_writer.jsonl` of the LLM cache is shared in git; real user accounts instead of the eight demo people.

## 4. Not verified

- **The full backend suite was last run before the final edits.** 122 tests passed after the pipeline and size changes. Edited after that and covered only by partial runs (fetch, foundation and signal tests pass): relevance filter, YouTube window and comment limit, thinking effort, cache keys. Run `cd backend && uv run pytest` (about 4 minutes, offline).
- **`npm run adapter-flow` passed (34 calls) before** the RAG, scoring and size changes. Run it again against a local database (see section 7).
- The screens were opened on real data once (login, brief, desk, case board, case page, requirement page, signals, audit). The vehicle plan page was only checked through its endpoint. The readable audit lines were checked in mock mode only.
- Database size on Supabase after the size changes: estimated, not measured.

## 5. Open work, in order

1. Finish and check the Supabase build (section 1).
2. Run the full test suite, then commit. Ask the user before committing. Include `backend/.data/llm_cache/feedback_classify.jsonl` (the shared cache now holds the real classifications) and decide with the user whether `case_writer.jsonl` is shared too.
3. Update the design documents. Only `changes.md` reflects this session. Still describing the old state: `database-design.md` (source of truth for tables), `data-model.mmd`, `INTEGRATION-GUIDE.md`, `backend/API.md`, `CLAUDE.md` (current phase, models, embedding size), `plan.md`, `web/README.md`.
4. Switch the UI to the Supabase-backed API: run the API with `AUTH_MODE=dev` (or Supabase tokens), `web/.env.local` with `DATA_SOURCE=backend` and `BACKEND_URL`. The demo users have fixed ids (`backend/app/demo.py`).
5. YouTube comments into Supabase. Proposed to the user, **not confirmed**: `uv run python -m app.fetch.worker --sources youtube-comments` (about 3,000 of 10,000 daily quota units, at most 1,500 comments). Ask first.
6. Try `requirement_writer@v2` and `rag_agent@v2` with OpenAI on one confirmed case before the demo.

## 6. Known problems

- **Fetch sources** (`backend/reports/fetch_smoke.md`, live check with `python -m app.fetch.smoke`): 32 of 81 returned records. 34 were reachable but returned nothing for the 5 Series; it is not known whether the parser misses the content or no article named the car. Blocked: `kbb`, `whatcar` (403), `autoscout24` (robots.txt). Broken: `press-lexus` (TLS handshake), `google-trends` (the library fails with the installed urllib3, `method_whitelist`). YouTube transcripts: every download answered `IpBlocked` from this machine.

"""Validation gate: every proposed signal passes these checks before it counts.

Order (plan.md phase 3): schema -> record exists -> quote found in the record ->
kind / severity / topic / aspect group consistent -> duplicate -> source known -> competitor
fact dated -> vehicle role from on_sale_since -> scope tag.

A failed check quarantines the signal with the reason; it is stored (visible in
the quarantine view), never silently dropped. The per-config source filter is
applied when reading (case figures, boards), not here, because one signal can
serve several configs.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as dt
import re
import unicodedata
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from pydantic import ValidationError

from app.signals.schema import SCHEMA_VERSION, SignalIn, severity_fits_kind

OUT_OF_SCOPE = re.compile(
    r"\b(homologation|type approval|regulat\w*|emission standard|euro 7|price|pricing|msrp|cost(s)? too|"
    r"lease rate|financing|insurance premium)\b",
    re.I,
)

_QUOTES = {"‘": "'", "’": "'", "“": '"', "”": '"', "–": "-", "—": "-", " ": " "}


@dataclass
class GateContext:
    records: dict[str, dict]
    topics: dict[str, dict]  # topic_id -> feature row (id, car_area, taxonomy_version)
    aspect_groups: set[str]
    sources: set[str]
    on_sale_since: dict[str, dt.date]
    competitors: set[str]
    existing: set[tuple] = field(default_factory=set)  # (record_id, kind, quote, topic or feature_hint)
    authored: dict[tuple, str] = field(default_factory=dict)  # (source_id, author_hash, quote) -> record_id


@dataclass
class GateResult:
    row: dict | None  # None = not storable (no record to attach the quarantine to)
    valid: bool
    reason: str | None = None


def load_context(conn, record_ids: set[str]) -> GateContext:
    records = {}
    if record_ids:
        for r in conn.execute(
            "select record_id, source_id, text_original, published_at, author_hash, market, country,"
            " vehicle_role, deleted_at from source_record where record_id = any(%s)",
            (list(record_ids),),
        ).fetchall():
            records[r["record_id"]] = r
    existing = set()
    authored = {}
    if record_ids:
        for s in conn.execute(
            "select s.record_id, s.kind, s.quote, coalesce(f.topic_id, s.feature_hint) as feature_hint,"
            " r.source_id, r.author_hash from signal s"
            " join source_record r using (record_id) left join feature f on f.id = s.feature_id"
            " where s.validation = 'valid' and (s.record_id = any(%s) or r.author_hash in"
            " (select author_hash from source_record where record_id = any(%s) and author_hash is not null))",
            (list(record_ids), list(record_ids)),
        ).fetchall():
            existing.add((s["record_id"], s["kind"], normalize(s["quote"] or ""), normalize(s["feature_hint"] or "")))
            if s["author_hash"]:
                authored[(s["source_id"], s["author_hash"], normalize(s["quote"] or ""))] = s["record_id"]
    return GateContext(
        records=records,
        topics={r["topic_id"]: r for r in conn.execute(
            "select id, topic_id, car_area, taxonomy_version from feature where topic_id is not null"
            " and status <> 'rejected'").fetchall()},
        aspect_groups={r["code"] for r in conn.execute("select code from aspect_group").fetchall()},
        sources={r["source_id"] for r in conn.execute("select source_id from source_registry").fetchall()},
        on_sale_since={r["code"]: r["on_sale_since"] for r in conn.execute(
            "select code, on_sale_since from vehicle where on_sale_since is not null").fetchall()},
        competitors={str(r["id"]) for r in conn.execute("select id from competitor").fetchall()},
        existing=existing,
        authored=authored,
    )


def normalize(text: str) -> str:
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text)
    text = "".join(_QUOTES.get(ch, ch) for ch in text)
    return " ".join(text.split()).casefold()


def find_quote(quote: str, text: str) -> str | None:
    """Return the exact substring of text that matches quote (whitespace, quote marks
    and case may differ), or None. The returned span is what gets stored."""
    if quote in text:
        return quote
    target = normalize(quote)
    if not target:
        return None
    # Map each normalized character back to its position in the original text.
    norm_chars: list[str] = []
    positions: list[int] = []
    prev_space = True
    for i, ch in enumerate(unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text)):
        ch = _QUOTES.get(ch, ch)
        if ch.isspace():
            if prev_space:
                continue
            ch, prev_space = " ", True
        else:
            prev_space = False
        for c in ch.casefold():
            norm_chars.append(c)
            positions.append(i)
    joined = "".join(norm_chars)
    idx = joined.find(target)
    if idx < 0 or len(unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text)) != len(text):
        return None

        " and not exists (select 1 from signal s where s.record_id = r.record_id)"

    by_source: dict[str, int] = {}

"""Daily fetch loop: python -m app.fetch.worker [--backfill] [--steps 1-9]

For every enabled source of the requested fetch steps (source_registry), and
every subject (BMW lines first when they have open cases, then competitors):
fetch -> store raw response + records (audited) -> agents propose signals ->
validation gate -> feature / case linking -> figures -> rescoring ->
notifications. One agent_run per source. New evidence on a confirmed case only
raises its flag. ``--dry-run`` writes the source list and the expected request
volume (phase 8 checkpoint) without fetching.

Run daily with cron, e.g. ``0 3 * * * cd backend && uv run python -m app.fetch.worker``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import traceback

from app import audit, db
from app.config import BACKEND_DIR, get_settings
from app.fetch import agents, subjects as subjects_mod
from app.fetch.adapters import api, downloads, feeds, libraries, scrape, sites  # noqa: F401  (registers adapters)
from app.fetch.adapters.base import ADAPTERS, FetchContext, FetchResult, NotConfigured
from app.fetch.http import BudgetExhausted, PoliteClient

PLAN_REPORT = BACKEND_DIR / "reports" / "fetch_plan.md"
# Sources fetched once per run for all subjects (feeds, newsrooms, market pages, app stores).
SHARED = feeds.SHARED | sites.SHARED | libraries.SHARED

# Rough requests per subject (incremental, backfill) for the dry-run estimate.
ESTIMATE = {
    "wikipedia": (1, 1), "wikidata": (1, 1), "nhtsa-vpic": (4, 4), "fueleconomy": (4, 4),
    "nhtsa-complaints": (12, 12), "nhtsa-recalls": (12, 12), "reddit": (16, 160), "youtube-comments": (20, 200),
    "tmc": (10, 2000), "genesis-owners": (10, 2000), "lucid-owners": (10, 400), "kbb": (2, 2),
    "motor-talk": (21, 4000), "pistonheads": (5, 1000), "carcomplaints": (10, 60),
    "ams": (1 + 10, 1 + 200), "autobild": (1 + 10, 1 + 200), "adac-autotest": (1 + 10, 1 + 200),
    "autoscout24": (1 + 10, 1 + 200), "youtube-transcripts": (20, 20),
}
SLUG_SOURCES = {"kbb", "motor-talk", "pistonheads", "carcomplaints"}


def parse_steps(text: str) -> list[int]:
    out = []
    for part in text.split(","):
        a, _, b = part.partition("-")
        out += list(range(int(a), int(b or a) + 1))
    return out


def _sources(conn, steps: list[int], only: list[str] | None) -> list[dict]:
    rows = conn.execute(
        "select r.*, (select max(ended_at) from agent_run a where a.agent = 'fetch:' || r.source_id"
        " and a.status in ('ok', 'partial')) as last_run_at"
        " from source_registry r where enabled and fetch_step = any(%s) order by fetch_step, source_id",
        (steps,)).fetchall()
    return [r for r in rows if not only or r["source_id"] in only]


def is_due(source: dict, now=None) -> bool:
    """A source runs when its last successful run is at least refresh_days old (cadence, changes.md 8.8)."""
    import datetime as dt

    if source.get("last_run_at") is None:
        return True
    now = now or dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc)
    # Half a day of slack so a daily cron at a slightly earlier time still runs.
    return now - source["last_run_at"] >= dt.timedelta(days=int(source.get("refresh_days") or 1), hours=-12)


def in_market(source: dict, subject) -> bool:
    """Country-specific sources only for subjects sold in that market (NHTSA, KBB, Motor-Talk, ...)."""
    from app.seed.loaders import country_to_market

    country = (source.get("country") or "").strip()
    if not country or not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Z]{2}", country) or not subject.markets:
        return True  # Global, per-country or unknown: no filter
    return country_to_market(country) in subject.markets


def _store(conn, result: FetchResult, actor: str, run_id) -> list[dict]:
    new = audit.insert_many_returning(conn, "source_record", result.records, actor=actor, key="record_id",
                                      run_id=run_id, on_conflict_do_nothing=True,
                                      rationale="fetched record (raw response in storage)")
    data = [d for d in result.data_records if d["value"] is not None or d["value_text"]]
    audit.insert_many(conn, "data_record", data, actor=actor, key="record_id", run_id=run_id,
                      on_conflict_do_nothing=True, rationale="fetched data record")
    return new


INGEST_BATCH = 25


def ingest_extracted(conn, extracted: list[tuple], run_id) -> dict:
    """Store what the agents proposed for records they have already read."""
    from app.signals import service

    totals = {"valid": 0, "quarantined": 0, "dropped": 0, "not_relevant": 0}
    for record, proposals, model, prompt_version in extracted:
        kept = 0
        if proposals:
            out = service.ingest(conn, proposals, actor=agents.agent_for(record), run_id=run_id,
                                 prompt_version=prompt_version, model=model)
            for k in ("valid", "quarantined", "dropped"):
                totals[k] += out[k]
            kept = out["valid"] + out["quarantined"]
        if kept == 0 and model is not None:
            # Relevance filter: the LLM read the record and found no statement about a feature of
            # the line or its competitors. Its text is not kept; the row stays as a marker (so the
            # record is not fetched and read again) and the run counts it. Without an LLM nothing
            # is judged, so nothing is purged.
            audit.tombstone(conn, "source_record", {"record_id": record["record_id"]},
                            ("text_original", "text_en", "title"), actor=agents.agent_for(record),
                            rationale="relevance filter: no statement about a tracked feature; text not kept")
            totals["not_relevant"] += 1
    return totals


def run_agents(conn, records: list[dict], run_id) -> dict:
    return ingest_extracted(conn, agents.extract_many(records), run_id)


def fetch_source(conn_factory, client: PoliteClient, source: dict, subjects: list, backfill: bool,
                 with_agents: bool) -> dict:
    sid = source["source_id"]
    with conn_factory() as conn:
        run_id = conn.execute("insert into agent_run (agent, mode, params) values (%s, %s, %s) returning id",
                              (f"fetch:{sid}", "backfill" if backfill else "incremental",
                               json.dumps({"step": source["fetch_step"]}))).fetchone()["id"]
    ctx = FetchContext(client=client, backfill=backfill, run_id=run_id)
    cursor = dict(source["last_cursor"] or {})
    summary = {"source": sid, "records": 0, "signals": {}, "requests": 0, "notes": []}
    status, error = "ok", None
    try:
        results: list[FetchResult] = []
        if sid in SHARED:
            results.append(SHARED[sid](ctx, source, subjects, cursor))
        elif (source["access"] or "").startswith("Download"):
            results.append(downloads.fetch_downloads(ctx, source, subjects, cursor))
        elif sid in ADAPTERS:
            for s in [s for s in subjects if in_market(source, s)]:
                results.append(ADAPTERS[sid](ctx, source, s, cursor))
        else:
            raise NotConfigured(f"no adapter for {sid} (access {source['access']})")
        with conn_factory() as conn:
            new_records = []
            for r in results:
                new_records += _store(conn, r, f"fetch:{sid}", run_id)
                cursor.update(r.cursor)
                summary["requests"] += r.requests
                summary["notes"] += r.notes
            summary["records"] = len(new_records)
            changes = {"last_cursor": cursor}
            if backfill:
                import datetime as dt

                changes["backfill_done_at"] = dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc)
            audit.update(conn, "source_registry", {"source_id": sid}, changes, actor="system", run_id=run_id,
                         rationale="fetch cursor after run")
        if with_agents and new_records:
            # The agents read outside the database transaction, in parallel; their signals are
            # then stored in short transactions.
            extracted = agents.extract_many(new_records)
            totals: dict = {}
            for i in range(0, len(extracted), INGEST_BATCH):
                with conn_factory() as conn:
                    for k, v in ingest_extracted(conn, extracted[i:i + INGEST_BATCH], run_id).items():
                        totals[k] = totals.get(k, 0) + v
            summary["signals"] = totals
    except NotConfigured as exc:
        status, error = "partial", str(exc)
        summary["notes"].append(error)
    except BudgetExhausted as exc:
        status, error = "partial", str(exc)
        summary["notes"].append(error)
    except Exception as exc:  # one failing source must not stop the loop
        status, error = "failed", f"{exc!r}\n{traceback.format_exc()[-1500:]}"
    with conn_factory() as conn:
        sig = summary["signals"] or {}
        conn.execute("update agent_run set status = %s, ended_at = now(), error = %s, records_fetched = %s,"
                     " signals_valid = %s, signals_quarantined = %s, params = params || %s where id = %s",
                     (status, error, summary["records"], sig.get("valid", 0), sig.get("quarantined", 0),
                      json.dumps({"requests": summary["requests"], "notes": summary["notes"][:20],
                                  "not_relevant": sig.get("not_relevant", 0)}), run_id))
        if status == "failed":
            audit.insert(conn, "notification", {"type": "run_failed", "object_type": "agent_run",
                                                "object_id": str(run_id), "message": f"fetch {sid} failed: {exc_text(error)}"},
                         actor="system")
    summary["status"] = status
    return summary


def exc_text(error: str | None) -> str:
    return (error or "").split("\n", 1)[0][:200]


def dry_run(steps: list[int], vehicles: list[str] | None, only: list[str] | None) -> str:
    with db.transaction() as conn:
        sources = _sources(conn, steps, only)
        subjects = subjects_mod.load(conn, vehicles)
    lines = ["# Fetch plan (dry run)", "",
             f"Steps {steps[0]} to {steps[-1]}; {len(subjects)} subjects "
             f"({sum(1 for s in subjects if s.kind == 'vehicle')} BMW lines, "
             f"{sum(1 for s in subjects if s.kind == 'competitor')} competitors).", "",
             "| Step | Source | Access | Adapter | Every (days) | Requests per run | Per day (average) | Backfill | Needs |",
             "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    tot_i = tot_b = 0
    tot_day = 0.0
    for s in sources:
        sid = s["source_id"]
        if sid in SHARED:
            inc, back = {"app-store": (17, 170), "google-play": (10, 100)}.get(
                sid, (1 + sites.MAX_ARTICLES, 1 + 200) if sid in sites.NEWSROOMS else (1, 1))
            adapter_name = SHARED[sid].__name__
        elif (s["access"] or "").startswith("Download"):
            inc = back = 0
            adapter_name = "download folder"
        elif sid in ADAPTERS:
            per = ESTIMATE.get(sid, (1, 1))
            slug_based = sid in scrape.MAGAZINES or sid in sites.MODEL_PAGES or sid in SLUG_SOURCES
            n = len([x for x in subjects if (not slug_based or x.slugs.get(sid)) and in_market(s, x)
                     and (sid not in scrape.FORUMS or x.label in scrape.FORUMS[sid])
                     and (not sid.startswith("youtube") or x.kind == "vehicle")])
            inc, back = per[0] * n, per[1] * n
            adapter_name = ADAPTERS[sid].__name__
        else:
            inc = back = 0
            adapter_name = "not built yet"
        settings = get_settings()
        needs = {"reddit": "" if settings.reddit_client_id else "Reddit OAuth app",
                 "youtube-comments": "" if settings.youtube_api_key else "YouTube Data API key",
                 "youtube-transcripts": "" if settings.youtube_api_key else "YouTube Data API key"}.get(sid, "")
        every = int(s.get("refresh_days") or 1)
        per_day = inc / every if not needs else 0.0
        tot_i += inc if not needs else 0
        tot_b += back
        tot_day += per_day
        lines.append(f"| {s['fetch_step']} | `{sid}` | {s['access']} | {adapter_name} | {every} | {inc} |"
                     f" {per_day:.0f} | {back} | {needs} |")
    lines += ["", f"Average: about {tot_day:.0f} requests per day (each source only when due, see 'Every'); "
              f"a day when every source is due would be about {tot_i}; the daily budget "
              f"FETCH_DAILY_REQUEST_BUDGET caps it either way, open cases first. One-time backfill: about {tot_b} "
              "requests, spread over days by the same budget (capped at 200 list pages per forum and subject). "
              "Sources that need a missing key are counted as 0.",
              "", "Politeness: robots.txt respected, at least 2 s between requests per host, retries with backoff, "
              "raw responses stored before parsing."]
    PLAN_REPORT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    PLAN_REPORT.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return str(PLAN_REPORT)


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--backfill", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--steps", default="1-9")
    parser.add_argument("--sources", default="")
    parser.add_argument("--vehicles", default="")
    parser.add_argument("--budget", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--no-agents", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--no-cases", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--force", action="store_true", help="run every selected source, due or not")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    steps = parse_steps(args.steps)
    only = [s for s in args.sources.split(",") if s] or None
    vehicles = [v for v in args.vehicles.split(",") if v] or None
    if args.dry_run:
        print(dry_run(steps, vehicles, only))
        return
    with db.transaction() as conn:
        sources = _sources(conn, steps, only)
        subjects = subjects_mod.load(conn, vehicles)
    client = PoliteClient(budget=args.budget)
    for source in sources:
        if not (args.force or args.backfill or only or is_due(source)):
            print({"source": source["source_id"], "status": "skipped", "reason": "not due"})
            continue
        if source["delay_seconds"]:
            client.default_delay = max(client.default_delay, float(source["delay_seconds"]))
        print(fetch_source(db.transaction, client, source, subjects, args.backfill, not args.no_agents))
    if not args.no_cases:
        from app.cases import pipeline
        from app.scoring import score

        print(pipeline.run(initial=False))
        with db.transaction() as conn:
            for cfg in conn.execute("select id from config where active").fetchall():
                score.score_config(conn, cfg["id"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Signal write path: gate -> embed -> store (valid or quarantined), and the
PM actions on the quarantine. Agents call ``ingest``; they never write cases."""

from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as dt

from app import audit, taxonomy
from app.llm.embeddings import get_embedder
from app.signals.gate import check, load_context

CONTENT_COLUMNS = ("summary", "quote", "quote_en", "feature_hint", "embedding")


def embedding_text(row: dict) -> str:
    """LLM summaries are embedded alone. Label-based seed summaries only repeat the
    BMW labels (and their kind), so feature hint + quote are embedded instead;
    otherwise clustering would split likes and complaints about the same problem
    (changes.md 3.2)."""
    if (row.get("extra") or {}).get("kind_source") in ("bmw_label", "heuristic"):
        return f"{row.get('feature_hint') or ''}. {(row.get('quote') or '')[:400]}".strip(". ")
    return row.get("summary") or ""


def ingest(conn, proposals: list[dict], *, actor: str, run_id=None, prompt_version=None, model=None) -> dict:
    """Validate and store proposed signals. Returns counts and the stored rows."""
    ctx = load_context(conn, {p.get("record_id") for p in proposals if p.get("record_id")})
    rows, dropped = [], []
    for p in proposals:
        result = check(p, ctx, run_id=run_id, prompt_version=prompt_version, model=model)
        if result.row is None:
            dropped.append(result.reason)
        else:
            rows.append(result.row)
    valid = [r for r in rows if r["validation"] == "valid"]
    if valid:
        embedder = get_embedder()
        vectors = embedder.embed([embedding_text(r) for r in valid])
        for r, v in zip(valid, vectors):
            r["embedding"] = v
            r["extra"] = {**(r.get("extra") or {}), "embedding_provider": embedder.name}
    columns = sorted({k for r in rows for k in r})
    rows = [{c: r.get(c) for c in columns} for r in rows]
    stored = audit.insert_many_returning(conn, "signal", rows, actor=actor, run_id=run_id,
                                         rationale="signal through the validation gate")
    queue_taxonomy_review(conn, actor=actor, run_id=run_id)
    return {
        "valid": sum(1 for r in stored if r["validation"] == "valid"),
        "quarantined": sum(1 for r in stored if r["validation"] == "quarantined"),
        "dropped": len(dropped),
        "dropped_reasons": dropped,
        "rows": stored,
    }


def queue_taxonomy_review(conn, *, actor: str, run_id=None) -> int:
    """Put valid signals with topic ``other`` or a low-confidence topic into the
    review queue (once each). A human resolves them; no topic is created here."""
    rows = conn.execute(
        "select s.id, f.topic_id, s.extra->>'other_suggestion' as suggestion from signal s"
        " join feature f on f.id = s.feature_id"
        " where s.validation = 'valid' and (f.topic_id = %s or s.classification_confidence = 'low')"
        " and not exists (select 1 from taxonomy_proposal p where p.signal_id = s.id)",
        (taxonomy.OTHER,),
    ).fetchall()
    return audit.insert_many(conn, "taxonomy_proposal", [
        {"signal_id": r["id"], "suggested_name": r["suggestion"],
         "reason": "other" if r["topic_id"] == taxonomy.OTHER else "low_confidence"} for r in rows
    ], actor=actor, run_id=run_id, rationale="classifier could not place the signal with confidence")


def delete_quarantined(conn, signal_id: str, *, actor: str, rationale: str, request_id=None) -> dict:
    """PM deletes a quarantined signal: content purged, tombstone kept. The source
    record is purged too when no other signal uses it."""
    row = conn.execute("select id, record_id, validation from signal where id = %s", (signal_id,)).fetchone()
    if row is None:
        raise audit.NotFound(f"signal {signal_id} not found")
    if row["validation"] != "quarantined":
        raise ValueError("only quarantined signals can be deleted here")
    out = audit.tombstone(conn, "signal", {"id": signal_id}, CONTENT_COLUMNS, actor=actor, rationale=rationale,

"""The signal contract: one statement about one topic from one source record.

Fixed core fields plus ``extra`` (source-specific), versioned by SCHEMA_VERSION.
Agents produce ``SignalIn``; the validation gate turns it into a stored row
(valid or quarantined). Field names follow fetching-sources.md section 7.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator

SCHEMA_VERSION = "signal@2"

Market = Literal["USA", "China", "Europe", "Rest of World", "unknown"]
Kind = Literal["complaint", "wish", "like", "competitor_fact", "trend", "innovation"]
Severity = Literal["defect", "difficult_to_use", "wish", "none"]
VehicleRole = Literal["current", "predecessor", "competitor", "unknown"]
EvidenceRole = Literal["bmw_customer", "competitor", "market"]
Powertrain = Literal["ICE", "PHEV", "BEV", "unknown"]
ReachUnit = Literal["views", "upvotes", "likes", "replies", "none"]

MAX_SUMMARY_WORDS = 20


class SignalIn(BaseModel):
    """What an agent (or the seed) proposes. Validated by the gate before storage."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    record_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
    kind: Kind
    severity: Severity = "none"
    summary: str = Field(min_length=3, description="English, at most 20 words")
    quote: str = Field(min_length=2, description="exact excerpt of the record text_original")
    quote_en: str | None = None
    # Closed taxonomy: the gate checks both against the stored lists and derives the
    # car area from the topic. No topic = waits for the LLM classifier.
    topic_id: str | None = None
    aspect_group: str | None = None
    classification_confidence: Literal["high", "medium", "low"] | None = None
    classified_by: Literal["bmw_label", "llm", "pm"] | None = None
    feature_hint: str | None = None
    evidence_role: EvidenceRole = "bmw_customer"
    market: Market = "unknown"
    market_basis: Literal["stated", "inferred", "unknown"] = "unknown"
    vehicle: str | None = None
    chassis_code: str | None = None
    competitor_id: str | None = None
    vehicle_role: VehicleRole = "unknown"
    powertrain: Powertrain = "unknown"
    customer_ref: str | None = None
    reach: int | None = Field(default=None, ge=0)
    reach_unit: ReachUnit = "none"
    data_record_id: str | None = None
    extra: dict = Field(default_factory=dict)

    @field_validator("summary")
    @classmethod
    def _short_summary(cls, v: str) -> str:
        v = " ".join(v.split())
        if len(v.split()) > MAX_SUMMARY_WORDS:
            raise ValueError(f"summary has more than {MAX_SUMMARY_WORDS} words")
        return v

    @field_validator("severity")
    @classmethod
    def _severity_known(cls, v: str) -> str:
        return v


def severity_fits_kind(kind: str, severity: str) -> bool:
    if kind == "complaint":
        return severity in ("defect", "difficult_to_use")
    if kind == "wish":
        return severity in ("wish", "none")
    return severity == "none"

content.content:
"""Scraped sources (plain HTTP, steps 5 to 7).

- XenForo forums (tmc, genesis-owners, lucid-owners): thread list -> threads ->
  posts, following ``<link rel="next">`` on every page (fetching-sources 3.9).
  One record per post.
- Expert review pages (magazines, step 7): one record per model page, URL from
  the slug of the subject on that site (fetching-sources 3.10).
- kbb: consumer reviews from the page's ``__NEXT_DATA__`` JSON.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from urllib.parse import urljoin

from selectolax.lexbor import LexborHTMLParser

from app.fetch.adapters.base import FetchContext, FetchResult, adapter, cursor_key
from app.fetch.records import text_record
from app.fetch.subjects import Subject, author_hash

# Forum per competitor, from fetching-sources.md 3.4 and 3.9.
FORUMS = {
    "tmc": {"Tesla Model S": "https://teslamotorsclub.com/tmc/forums/model-s.73/"},
    "genesis-owners": {
        "Genesis G80": "https://www.genesisowners.com/genesis-forum/forums/genesis-g80-forum-g80-ev-forum-g80forum-com.107/",
        "Genesis G90": "https://www.genesisowners.com/genesis-forum/forums/genesis-g90-2023-second-generation.161/",
    },
    "lucid-owners": {"Lucid Air": "https://lucidowners.com/forums/air-bugs-issues-support.134/"},
}
MAGAZINES = {
    "caranddriver": ("https://www.caranddriver.com/{slug}", "US", "en"),
    "motortrend": ("https://www.motortrend.com/cars/{slug}/", "US", "en"),
    "autocar": ("https://www.autocar.co.uk/car-review/{slug}", "GB", "en"),
    "autoexpress": ("https://www.autoexpress.co.uk/{slug}", "GB", "en"),
    "topgear": ("https://www.topgear.com/car-reviews/{slug}", "GB", "en"),
    "drive-uk": ("https://www.drive.co.uk/cars/{slug}/review", "GB", "en"),
    "whatcar": ("https://www.whatcar.com/{slug}/review/", "GB", "en"),
    "carwow": ("https://www.carwow.co.uk/{slug}", "GB", "en"),
    "parkers": ("https://www.parkers.co.uk/{slug}/review/", "GB", "en"),
}
_WS = re.compile(r"\s+")


def _html(text: str) -> LexborHTMLParser:
    return LexborHTMLParser(text)


def _next(tree, base: str) -> str | None:
    link = tree.css_first('link[rel="next"]')
    return urljoin(base, link.attributes["href"]) if link and link.attributes.get("href") else None


def parse_thread_list(html: str, base: str) -> tuple[list[dict], str | None]:
    tree = _html(html)
    threads = []
    for item in tree.css(".structItem--thread"):
        a = item.css_first(".structItem-title a[data-tp-primary]") or item.css_first(".structItem-title a")
        latest = item.css_first("time.structItem-latestDate")
        if a and a.attributes.get("href"):
            threads.append({"url": urljoin(base, a.attributes["href"]), "title": a.text(strip=True),
                            "latest": int(latest.attributes.get("data-timestamp", 0)) if latest else 0})
    return threads, _next(tree, base)


def parse_thread(html: str, base: str) -> tuple[list[dict], str | None]:
    tree = _html(html)
    title = tree.css_first("h1")
    posts = []
    for art in tree.css("article.message"):
        body = art.css_first(".bbWrapper")
        when = art.css_first("time.u-dt")
        if not body:
            continue
        for quote in body.css("blockquote"):  # quoted earlier posts are not this author's statement
            quote.decompose()
        text = _WS.sub(" ", body.text(separator=" ")).strip()
        if text:
            posts.append({"id": art.attributes.get("data-content", "").replace("post-", ""),
                          "author": art.attributes.get("data-author"), "text": text,
                          "published": when.attributes.get("datetime") if when else None,
                          "thread_title": title.text(strip=True) if title else None})
    return posts, _next(tree, base)


def _xenforo(ctx: FetchContext, source: dict, subject: Subject, cursor: dict) -> FetchResult:
    out = FetchResult()
    start = FORUMS.get(source["source_id"], {}).get(subject.label)
    if not start:
        return out
    newest_seen = int(cursor.get(cursor_key(subject), 0))
    top = newest_seen
    url, pages = start, 0
    host = re.match(r"https?://[^/]+", start).group(0)
    while url and pages < ctx.max_pages:
        r = ctx.client.get(url, source_id=source["source_id"])
        out.requests += 1
        pages += 1
        threads, url = parse_thread_list(r.text, host)
        if not ctx.backfill:
            threads = [t for t in threads if t["latest"] > newest_seen]
            if not threads:
                break
        for t in threads:
            top = max(top, t["latest"])
            turl, tpages = t["url"], 0
            while turl and tpages < (ctx.max_pages if ctx.backfill else 3):
                tr = ctx.client.get(turl, source_id=source["source_id"])
                out.requests += 1
                tpages += 1
                posts, turl = parse_thread(tr.text, host)
                thread_id = re.search(r"\.(\d+)/", t["url"]).group(1) if re.search(r"\.(\d+)/", t["url"]) else t["url"]
                for p in posts:
                    out.records.append(text_record(
                        source=source, subject=subject, record_id=f"{source['source_id']}-post-{p['id']}",
                        response=tr, text=p["text"], url=f"{t['url']}post-{p['id']}", category="C",
                        content_type="owner", title=p["thread_title"] or t["title"], published_at=p["published"],
                        search_term=subject.label, thread_id=thread_id,
                        author_hash=author_hash(source["source_id"], p["author"]), country="US",
                        run_id=ctx.run_id))
    out.cursor[cursor_key(subject)] = top
    return out


adapter("tmc", "genesis-owners", "lucid-owners")(_xenforo)


def article_text(html: str) -> tuple[str | None, str]:
    tree = _html(html)
    for bad in tree.css("script, style, nav, header, footer, aside, form, noscript"):
        bad.decompose()
    title = tree.css_first("h1")
    root = tree.css_first("article") or tree.css_first("main") or tree.body
    paragraphs = [_WS.sub(" ", p.text()).strip() for p in (root.css("p") if root else [])]
    text = "\n\n".join(p for p in paragraphs if len(p) > 40)
    return (title.text(strip=True) if title else None), text


def _magazine(ctx: FetchContext, source: dict, subject: Subject, cursor: dict) -> FetchResult:
    out = FetchResult()
    pattern, country, language = MAGAZINES[source["source_id"]]
    for slug in subject.slugs.get(source["source_id"], []):
        if slug.endswith("/reviews/") and source["source_id"] != "parkers":
            continue
        url = pattern.format(slug=slug.rstrip("/").removesuffix("/reviews"))
        r = ctx.client.get(url, source_id=source["source_id"])
        out.requests += 1
        if r.status != 200:
            out.notes.append(f"{url}: HTTP {r.status}")
            continue
        title, text = article_text(r.text)
        if len(text) < 200:
            out.notes.append(f"{url}: no article text found")
            continue
        out.records.append(text_record(
            source=source, subject=subject, record_id=f"{source['source_id']}-{slug.replace('/', '-')}",
            response=r, text=text, url=url, category="D", content_type="expert", title=title,
            search_term=slug, country=country, language=language, run_id=ctx.run_id))
    return out


adapter(*MAGAZINES)(_magazine)


def _find_reviews(node, found: list) -> None:
    """Walk __NEXT_DATA__ and collect objects that look like consumer reviews."""
    if isinstance(node, dict):
        keys = set(node)
        text_key = next((k for k in ("reviewText", "text", "body", "comments") if isinstance(node.get(k), str)), None)
        if text_key and keys & {"rating", "overallRating", "ratingValue", "stars"} and len(node[text_key]) > 40:
            found.append(node)
        for v in node.values():
            _find_reviews(v, found)
    elif isinstance(node, list):
        for v in node:
            _find_reviews(v, found)


@adapter("kbb")
def kbb(ctx: FetchContext, source: dict, subject: Subject, cursor: dict) -> FetchResult:
    out = FetchResult()
    for slug in subject.slugs.get("kbb", []):
        years = [slug.rsplit("/", 1)[1]] if re.search(r"/\d{4}$", slug) else ["2025", "2024"]
        base = re.sub(r"/\d{4}$", "", slug)
        for year in years:
            url = f"https://www.kbb.com/{base}/{year}/consumer-reviews/"
            r = ctx.client.get(url, source_id="kbb")
            out.requests += 1
            m = re.search(r'<script id="__NEXT_DATA__"[^>]*>(.*?)</script>', r.text, re.S)
            if not m:
                continue
            found: list = []
            _find_reviews(json.loads(m.group(1)), found)
            for i, rev in enumerate(found):
                text = next(rev[k] for k in ("reviewText", "text", "body", "comments") if isinstance(rev.get(k), str))
                rating = next((rev[k] for k in ("rating", "overallRating", "ratingValue", "stars") if k in rev), None)
                rid = rev.get("id") or rev.get("reviewId") or f"{year}-{i}"
                out.records.append(text_record(
                    source=source, subject=subject, record_id=f"kbb-{base.replace('/', '-')}-{rid}", response=r,
                    text=text, url=url, category="B", content_type="owner", title=rev.get("title"),
                    published_at=rev.get("date") or rev.get("submissionDate"), search_term=base, country="US",
                    rating_value=float(rating) if isinstance(rating, (int, float)) else None, rating_scale=5,
                    author_hash=author_hash("kbb", rev.get("author") or rev.get("nickname")),
                    model_year=year, run_id=ctx.run_id))
    return out
"""Polite HTTP for the fetch loop: robots.txt, per-host delay, user agent,
retries with backoff, a daily request budget, and the untouched raw response
saved to storage first (content-addressed ``raw_ref``).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import time
import urllib.robotparser
from dataclasses import dataclass
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

import httpx

from app import storage
from app.config import get_settings


class BudgetExhausted(RuntimeError):
    pass


class Disallowed(RuntimeError):
    """robots.txt forbids the URL."""


@dataclass
class Response:
    url: str
    status: int
    content: bytes
    content_type: str
    raw_ref: str
    fetched_at: float

    @property
    def text(self) -> str:
        return self.content.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")

    def json(self):
        import json

        return json.loads(self.content)


class PoliteClient:
    def __init__(self, *, budget: int | None = None, default_delay: float = 2.0, client: httpx.Client | None = None,
                 respect_robots: bool = True) -> None:
        s = get_settings()
        self.user_agent = s.fetch_user_agent
        self.budget = budget if budget is not None else s.fetch_daily_request_budget
        self.used = 0
        self.default_delay = default_delay
        self.delays: dict[str, float] = {}
        self._last: dict[str, float] = {}
        self._robots: dict[str, urllib.robotparser.RobotFileParser | None] = {}
        self.respect_robots = respect_robots
        self.client = client or httpx.Client(timeout=30, follow_redirects=True,
                                             headers={"User-Agent": self.user_agent})

    def _allowed(self, url: str) -> bool:
        if not self.respect_robots:
            return True
        parts = urlsplit(url)
        base = f"{parts.scheme}://{parts.netloc}"
        if base not in self._robots:
            parser = urllib.robotparser.RobotFileParser()
            try:
                r = self.client.get(base + "/robots.txt")
                self.used += 1
                if r.status_code >= 400:
                    parser = None
                else:
                    parser.parse(r.text.splitlines())
            except httpx.HTTPError:
                parser = None
            self._robots[base] = parser
        parser = self._robots[base]
        return True if parser is None else parser.can_fetch(self.user_agent, url)

    def _wait(self, host: str) -> None:
        delay = self.delays.get(host, self.default_delay)
        last = self._last.get(host)
        if last is not None:
            gap = time.monotonic() - last
            if gap < delay:
                time.sleep(delay - gap)
        self._last[host] = time.monotonic()

    def get(self, url: str, *, source_id: str, params: dict | None = None, headers: dict | None = None,
            retries: int = 3, official_api: bool = False) -> Response:
        """``official_api``: a documented public API meant for programs (e.g. the MediaWiki
        Action API). robots.txt speaks to crawlers of pages, so it is not consulted there."""
        if self.used >= self.budget:
            raise BudgetExhausted(f"daily request budget of {self.budget} used")
        params = {k: v for k, v in (params or {}).items() if v is not None}  # an unset parameter is not sent
        full = str(httpx.URL(url, params=params)) if params else url
        if not official_api and not self._allowed(full):

def german_date(text: str, today: dt.date | None = None) -> dt.datetime | None:
    """motor-talk: 'am 10. Oktober 2026 um 10:55 Uhr', 'heute um 09:12 Uhr', 'gestern um ...'."""
    today = today or dt.date.today()
    t = text.lower()
    time = re.search(r"(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})", t)

    if "heute" in t or "gestern" in t:

            return None
        d = dt.date(int(m.group(3)), GERMAN_MONTHS[m.group(2)], int(m.group(1)))

    t = text.lower()
    if t.startswith("today") or t.startswith("yesterday"):
        d = today - dt.timedelta(days=1 if t.startswith("yesterday") else 0)
        return dt.datetime(d.year, d.month, d.day, tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)
    m = re.search(r"(\d{1,2})(?:st|nd|rd|th)?\s+([a-z]+)(?:\s+(\d{4}))?", t)
    if m and m.group(2)[:3] in ENGLISH_MONTHS:
        day, month, year = int(m.group(1)), ENGLISH_MONTHS[m.group(2)[:3]], int(m.group(3) or today.year)

        m = re.search(r"([a-z]{3})[a-z]*\s+(\d{1,2})\s*(\d{4})", t)

"""Polite HTTP for the fetch loop: robots.txt, per-host delay, user agent,
retries with backoff, a daily request budget, and the untouched raw response
saved to storage first (content-addressed ``raw_ref``).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import time
import urllib.robotparser
from dataclasses import dataclass
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

import httpx

from app import storage
from app.config import get_settings


class BudgetExhausted(RuntimeError):
    pass


class Disallowed(RuntimeError):
    """robots.txt forbids the URL."""


@dataclass
class Response:
    url: str
    status: int
    content: bytes
    content_type: str
    raw_ref: str
    fetched_at: float

    @property
    def text(self) -> str:
        return self.content.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")

    def json(self):
        import json

        return json.loads(self.content)


class PoliteClient:
    def __init__(self, *, budget: int | None = None, default_delay: float = 2.0, client: httpx.Client | None = None,
                 respect_robots: bool = True) -> None:
        s = get_settings()
        self.user_agent = s.fetch_user_agent
        self.budget = budget if budget is not None else s.fetch_daily_request_budget
        self.used = 0
        self.default_delay = default_delay
        self.delays: dict[str, float] = {}
        self._last: dict[str, float] = {}
        self._robots: dict[str, urllib.robotparser.RobotFileParser | None] = {}
        self.respect_robots = respect_robots
        self.client = client or httpx.Client(timeout=30, follow_redirects=True,
                                             headers={"User-Agent": self.user_agent})

    def _allowed(self, url: str) -> bool:
        if not self.respect_robots:
            return True
        parts = urlsplit(url)
        base = f"{parts.scheme}://{parts.netloc}"
        if base not in self._robots:
            parser = urllib.robotparser.RobotFileParser()
            try:
                r = self.client.get(base + "/robots.txt")
                self.used += 1
                if r.status_code >= 400:
                    parser = None
                else:
                    parser.parse(r.text.splitlines())
            except httpx.HTTPError:
                parser = None
            self._robots[base] = parser
        parser = self._robots[base]
        return True if parser is None else parser.can_fetch(self.user_agent, url)

    def _wait(self, host: str) -> None:
        delay = self.delays.get(host, self.default_delay)
        last = self._last.get(host)
        if last is not None:
            gap = time.monotonic() - last
            if gap < delay:
                time.sleep(delay - gap)
        self._last[host] = time.monotonic()

    def get(self, url: str, *, source_id: str, params: dict | None = None, headers: dict | None = None,
            retries: int = 3, official_api: bool = False) -> Response:
        """``official_api``: a documented public API meant for programs (e.g. the MediaWiki
        Action API). robots.txt speaks to crawlers of pages, so it is not consulted there."""
        if self.used >= self.budget:
            raise BudgetExhausted(f"daily request budget of {self.budget} used")
        params = {k: v for k, v in (params or {}).items() if v is not None}  # an unset parameter is not sent
        full = str(httpx.URL(url, params=params)) if params else url
        if not official_api and not self._allowed(full):
            raise Disallowed(full)
        host = urlsplit(full).netloc
        attempt = 0
        while True:
            self._wait(host)
            self.used += 1
            try:
                r = self.client.get(full, headers=headers)
            except httpx.HTTPError:
                if attempt >= retries:
                    raise
                attempt += 1
                time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
                continue
            if r.status_code in (429, 500, 502, 503, 504) and attempt < retries:
                attempt += 1
                retry_after = r.headers.get("retry-after")
                time.sleep(float(retry_after) if retry_after and retry_after.isdigit() else 2 ** attempt * 2)
                continue
            break
        content = r.content
        digest = hashlib.sha256(content).hexdigest()
        day = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d", time.gmtime())
        raw_ref = f"{source_id}/{day}/{digest[:2]}/{digest}"
        if not storage.exists(raw_ref):
            storage.put(raw_ref, content, r.headers.get("content-type", "application/octet-stream"))
        return Response(full, r.status_code, content, r.headers.get("content-type", ""), raw_ref, time.time())

def names_subject(text: str, terms: list[str]) -> str | None:
    lowered = text.lower()
    for t in terms:
        if re.search(r"(?<![\w])" + re.escape(t) + r"(?![\w])", lowered):
            return t
    return None

def german_date(text: str, today: dt.date | None = None) -> dt.datetime | None:
    """motor-talk: 'am 10. Oktober 2026 um 10:55 Uhr', 'heute um 09:12 Uhr', 'gestern um ...'."""
    today = today or dt.date.today()
    t = text.lower()
    time = re.search(r"(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})", t)
    hh, mm = (int(time.group(1)), int(time.group(2))) if time else (0, 0)
    if "heute" in t or "gestern" in t:
        d = today - dt.timedelta(days=1 if "gestern" in t else 0)
    else:
        m = re.search(r"(\d{1,2})\.\s*([a-zäöü]+)\s+(\d{4})", t)
        if not m or m.group(2) not in GERMAN_MONTHS:
            return None
        d = dt.date(int(m.group(3)), GERMAN_MONTHS[m.group(2)], int(m.group(1)))
    return dt.datetime(d.year, d.month, d.day, hh, mm, tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)


def english_date(text: str, today: dt.date | None = None) -> dt.datetime | None:
    """pistonheads 'Monday 14th April 2025', 'Monday 5th October' (this year), 'Yesterday (22:15)';
    carcomplaints 'Sep 20 2016'."""
    today = today or dt.date.today()
    t = text.lower()
    if t.startswith("today") or t.startswith("yesterday"):
        d = today - dt.timedelta(days=1 if t.startswith("yesterday") else 0)
        return dt.datetime(d.year, d.month, d.day, tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)
    m = re.search(r"(\d{1,2})(?:st|nd|rd|th)?\s+([a-z]+)(?:\s+(\d{4}))?", t)
    if m and m.group(2)[:3] in ENGLISH_MONTHS:
        day, month, year = int(m.group(1)), ENGLISH_MONTHS[m.group(2)[:3]], int(m.group(3) or today.year)
    else:
        m = re.search(r"([a-z]{3})[a-z]*\s+(\d{1,2})\s*(\d{4})", t)
        if not m or m.group(1) not in ENGLISH_MONTHS:
            return None
        day, month, year = int(m.group(2)), ENGLISH_MONTHS[m.group(1)], int(m.group(3))
    try:
        return dt.datetime(year, month, day, tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)
    except ValueError:
        return None

def article_links(html: str, page_url: str, terms: list[str], path_hint: str | None = None) -> list[str]:
    """Same-host links whose text or URL names the subject (or contains the model
    slug), without fragments, the page itself or obvious navigation."""
    host = urlsplit(page_url).netloc
    out = []
    for a in _tree(html).css("a"):
        href = (a.attributes.get("href") or "").split("#")[0]
        if not href or href.startswith(("mailto:", "javascript:")):
            continue
        url = urljoin(page_url, href)
        parts = urlsplit(url)
        if parts.netloc != host or url.rstrip("/") == page_url.rstrip("/") or parts.path.count("/") < 2:
            continue
        label = f"{_text(a)} {parts.path.replace('-', ' ')} {parts.path}"
        if names_subject(label, terms) or (path_hint and path_hint in parts.path.lower()
                                           and parts.path.rstrip("/").lower() != path_hint):
            out.append(url)
    return list(dict.fromkeys(out))

        title, text = article_text(r.text)

            out.records.append(text_record(

                url=url, category=category, content_type=content_type, title=title, published_at=None,
                search_term=slug, country=country, language=language, run_id=ctx.run_id))
        if not follow:
            continue
        links = [u for u in article_links(r.text, url, terms, "/" + slug.split("/")[-1].lower())

        for link in links:
